To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) a single run of a benchmark is insufficient for rigorous evaluation and (2) the current practice of running the same benchmark multiple times is inefficient.

(1) the time required to run benchmarks can be reduced by a factor of 2-10, (2) the time required for VM invocations can be reduced by an order of magnitude, (3) the time required by benchmark builds can be reduced by up to 50%, (4) the time required per benchmark iteration can be reduced by more than 50%, and (5) the time required overall can be reduced by 2 orders of magnitude

(a) we propose a new benchmarking framework that allows for a rigorous statistical analysis of the results; (b) we show how to use it to obtain statistically significant results in reasonable time; (c) we show that the proposed framework is useful in a number of scenarios, such as the evaluation of a new compiler, the evaluation of a virtual machine, the evaluation of an operating system, and the comparison of two different operating systems.
